title: Tenant memory surge: failure-mode analysis and runtime stitcher hotfix
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported intermittent GPU OOMs over the past two weeks. Investigation showed a correlated memory surge pattern where ephemeral session allocations plus a slow-growing KV cache leak combined with allocator fragmentation led to long-tail unusable GPU memory. This ticket tracked triage, a temporary mitigation for affected clusters, a runtime 'stitcher' patch to prevent arena siloing and a staged rollout across environments.
impact_summary: 3 high-revenue customers experienced degraded inference availability (5–25% request fail-rate during surge windows) across 6 clusters. Latency increased on affected nodes due to repeated OOM retries and fallback routing, causing visible SLA slips for Dedicated customers and escalations from two enterprise support tickets.
root_cause: A chain of events: (1) a small leak in the KV cache metadata path allowed per-session descriptors to persist beyond session end, (2) the new stride allocator introduced in runtime-1.18 created isolated arenas for large ephemeral tensors which prevented normal coalescing, and (3) a race between async evict heartbeats and session sweep left tombstoned KV handles that pinned slab extents. The combination produced high external fragmentation and transient resident allocations that the GPU driver treated as used memory, triggering OOM despite unused logical capacity.
steps_to_reproduce: Start a mixed load with many short sessions (1000s/min) enforcing repeated long-history KV lookups
Enable the new stride allocator via config used in runtime-1.18 (alloc.mode=stride) and set low eviction thresholds (kv.eviction_low=0.15)
Observe memory growth and slab fragmentation after ~1–3 hours under sustained burst; trigger by instrumented replay harness linked in artifacts
temporary_mitigations: Immediate: Increased kv.eviction_low to 0.35 on affected clusters to force more aggressive compaction
Rollback: Reverted stride allocator for the most impacted Dedicated pools to the legacy arena fallback (config change) to allow coalescing
Autoscale: Enabled conservative burst-capacity policy for Hosted customers to mask OOM symptoms while patch validated
permanent_fix_summary: Implemented 'stitcher' runtime hotfix: when arena fragmentation crosses a threshold the stitcher will proactively migrate freed slab pages into a reclaimable super-arena and repair dangling KV metadata by reconciling tombstones during a background pass. Also fixed the KV metadata leak by ensuring session-descriptor finalizers run after async evict callbacks complete.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: We chose background migration (stitcher) over synchronous compaction to avoid adding tail-latency to inference requests. Background passes are rate-limited and checkpoint-safe; that accepts a small window of elevated fragmentation in exchange for stable p99 latency. We delayed introducing a kernel-level defragmentation to avoid hardware-specific driver interactions during the rollout.
rollout_plan: Canary: Deploy hotfix to 3 lowest-traffic Hosted regions and one Dedicated QA pool (2026-03-07)
Monitor: 72-hour canary with p50/p95/p99 memory and OOM counters, KV tombstone rate, and customer error rates
Gradual: If canary stable, batch deploy to remaining Hosted clusters over 24 hours, then Dedicated (staged by tenant size), then advisory for Private customers with on-prem packages
Backout: config flag runtime.stitcher.enabled=false and revert kv metadata change if unexpected regressions observed
test_plan: Unit tests: verify finalizer ordering and tombstone reconciliation semantics
Integration: 24h load tests using replay harness that reproduces fragmentation pattern (artifact link below)
Chaos: inject delayed evict callbacks and elevated session churn to validate stitcher stability
Regression: ensure token-level latency p99 does not increase beyond +5% in synthetic benchmarks
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: fragmentation_ratio > 0.7 for > 15m AND kv.tombstone_rate increasing => P0 pager
Dashboards: per-tenant memory topology view and GPU resident heatmap added to Console runtime dashboard
postmortem_actions: Ship runtime-1.19.3-hotfix with stitcher and leak fix (completed)
Run a 2-week post-deploy study to confirm no recurrence and tune stitcher thresholds
Add an automated canary test to CI that reproduces high churn KV pattern before runtime releases
Document postmortem summary for affected customers and attach remediation notes to support tickets
